capabilities: Suggest notes inline while typing a two-character or longer prefix
Replace the typed word with a [[note path|keyword]] link
Restrict suggestion scope by folder path and tag
Index note titles and frontmatter aliases
Rank up to eight suggestions by recency and cumulative link frequency
extras: The README states the plugin is a personal learning project that is no longer actively maintained or expanded, and recommends Various Complements for everyday use. Extensive performance profiling data and design trade-off notes (Trie over fuzzy matching, memory-for-responsiveness caching) are included.
motivation: The author built it as a personal project to explore real-time recommendation with data structures, external-API boundaries, TDD, Electron profiling, and CI/CD.
problem: Obsidian's native internal linking requires typing [[ and finding a note in a search popup, an unnecessary context switch when the related concept is already in mind while writing.

relations.evidence: For everyday use, consider the actively maintained Various Complements.

summary: Inline autocomplete that suggests notes matching the word being typed and replaces it with an internal link, scoped by folder paths and tags.
